subject: <subject, e.g. Mathematics>
standard: <optional: standard/objective code or text this lesson targets>
source_lesson_summary: <brief description of the EXISTING lesson this plan differentiates -- this skill adapts a lesson that already exists, it does not create a new one from scratch>
learner_needs: <optional free text: ELL/WIDA levels, IEP goal areas, 504 accommodations, or other specific student needs to factor into the Below tier -- not validated, pass-through only>

shared.essential_question: <the single core learning goal/essential question -- identical for every tier by construction, since it lives here once instead of being retyped per tier>

core_tasks.task: <core task/problem text -- the same task context every tier's worksheet references, so tiers cannot drift apart on WHAT students are working on, only HOW>

shared.reflect_prompt: <one open-ended reflective prompt required on every tier's worksheet, e.g. 'Explain your thinking' or 'What strategy did you use and why?'>
shared.anchor_activity: <optional: a standard-aligned early-finisher task, printed on every tier's worksheet -- not busywork>

below.entry_point: <where Below-tier students start relative to the core task -- e.g. one step back from the grade-level entry point>
scaffolds: <scaffold 1, e.g. a sentence starter, a worked first step, a visual/manipulative support>

worksheet_items.modification: <how this core task is presented differently for Below -- e.g. broken into smaller steps, with a sentence frame>

above.entry_point: <where Above-tier students start relative to the core task -- e.g. skipping the scaffolded entry, straight into open-ended application>
above.extension: <the genuine extension task for Above -- a qualitatively different challenge (more variables, open-ended justification, real-world transfer), never just 'more of the same' problems>

worksheet_items.modification: <how this core task is extended for Above -- e.g. an added constraint or a 'justify your answer' requirement>
